messages.author: a2d9b83cabaa80ae
messages.subject: error message when trying to fit a relatively simple model
parts:
I'm trying to replicate Model 2 in Gignac (2006) (link to paper at the end of this message) but getting the following error message when fitting the model: 

Error in tmp[cbind(REP$row[idx], REP$col[idx])] <- lavpartable$free[idx] : 
  NAs are not allowed in subscripted assignments

This has been reported in a couple of other messages on this forum but no answers appear. I've installed the latest versions of R and lavaan. Here's the model statement: 

Model2 <- 'EI =~ Rep + Clar + Att + EOT + DDF + DIF
           TAS =~ EOT + DDF + DIF
           TAS ~~ 0*EI
           Rep ~~ Clar
           Att ~~ EOT
           Rep ~~ Att
           Att ~~ SWLS 
           SWLS ~ EI   
'
If I remove either of these two residual covariances: Rep ~~ Att  or Att ~~ SWLS, the error message does not appear. 

Here is the data and model fitting statement: 

names <- c("SWLS", "PA", "NA", "TMMS", "Att", "Clar", "Rep", "TAS20", "DIF", "DDF", "EOT")
R <- getCov("1.00
             0.55  1.00
             0.44 -0.31  1.00
             0.26  0.32 -0.19  1.00
             0.02  0.22  0.01  0.78  1.00
             0.45  0.37 -0.35  0.67  0.18  1.00
             0.16  0.12 -0.13  0.74  0.37  0.41  1.00
            -0.26 -0.13  0.31 -0.42 -0.36 -0.37 -0.17   1.00
            -0.32 -0.15  0.46 -0.26 -0.17 -0.30 -0.09   0.77  1.00
            -0.18 -0.11  0.17 -0.31 -0.26 -0.33 -0.06   0.78  0.45  1.00
            -0.08 -0.04  0.04 -0.39 -0.39 -0.21 -0.22   0.73  0.24  0.43  1.00",
            names = names)
mu <- c(23.64, 21.24, 14.06, 83.51, 38.01, 23.91, 21.59, 45.66, 13.62, 12.18, 19.84)
SD <- c(12.22, 4.96, 3.20, 10.63, 6.10, 4.49, 3.80, 11.05, 5.46, 4.10, 4.98)
S <- cor2cov(R = R, sds = SD, names = names)
n <- 107

fitMod2 <- sem(Model2, sample.cov = S, sample.nobs = n, std.lv = TRUE)

--- 

If it helps, I successfully replicated his Model 1 and got exactly matching results. Given that Gignac reports results for this Model in his paper, I assume that it should be identified. If anyone has any tips as to what that error message could indicate, I'll be so grateful! 

Best,
Mijke

link to the paper (Gignac, 2006): https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Gilles_Gignac/publication/238293403_Self-reported_emotional_intelligence_and_life_satisfaction_Testing_incremental_predictive_validity_hypotheses_via_structural_equation_modeling_SEM_in_a_small_sample/links/5a3503b40f7e9b10d843aead/Self-reported-emotional-intelligence-and-life-satisfaction-Testing-incremental-predictive-validity-hypotheses-via-structural-equation-modeling-SEM-in-a-small-sample.pdf

Mijke--
     There is a strong risk of empirical underidentification here, and the problem might crop up during iterative estimation. You might sidestep that using starting values, and maybe Gignac's final estimates would work as starting values for you. However, if any of the three loadings on TAS are smaller than Gignac's lowest 0.31, then identification may well fail, particularly at your low n.
--Ed Rigdon

parts:
Thanks, Ed. 

I'm using the same dataset that Gignac uses (and the parameter estimates for Model 1 match his exactly). Are you sure that this error indicates an identification problem? Starting values didn't help, and now I've tried fixing the parameter values to Gignac's values (i.e., estimating nothing but residual variances) and I am still getting the same error message:

Model2 <- 'EI =~ .19*Rep + .68*Clar + .33*Att + .24*EOT + .46*DDF + .48*DIF
           TAS =~ .39*EOT + .75*DDF + .31*DIF
           TAS ~~ 0*EI
           Rep ~~ .41*Clar
           Att ~~ .25*EOT
           Rep ~~ 0.32*Att
           Att ~~ -.24*SWLS
           SWLS ~ .61*EI  
'
fitMod2 <- sem(Model2, sample.cov = R, sample.nobs = n, std.lv = TRUE)

I wish I knew where in the estimation process it occurs... 

Mijke

messages.subject: Re: error message when trying to fit a relatively simple model
parts:
Mijke--
     OK, that didn't work, and I'm fishing. These are fully standardized parameter estimates, yes? Which would mean that the factors have variances of 1. (What do the estimated variances look like in the solution, when you get this error message?) What if you set those factor variances to 1 explicitly? Sure, you DF will be off by the number of fixed parameter estimates. But if this doesn't work, then I'm thinking you (or Gignac) have a typo that has escaped our eyes. The negative residual covariance looks fishy to me, but Gignac is consistent on that across Models 2 and 3.
     In Model 2, SWLS is just another indicator of EI, with residual covariances, even though it has been swung to the right. It is hard to intuit with such a complex model.
--Ed Rigdon

Ed, you're brilliant. When I change the model statement to specify SWLS as an indicator of EI (rather than regressing it on EI later) the model runs and perfectly reproduces his results. 

I was fishing too and had gotten this far:  
- the problem arises when I simulate data from (the original) Model 2. None of the parameter values matter. 
- The problem arises within the internal lav_model function. (So before anything is estimated, I think). I broke it down to run line by line, and it gets to this line within the mm loop where mm == 3

tmp[ cbind(REP$row[idx], REP$col[idx]) ] <- parTable2$free[idx]

which doesn't work because 

> REP$row[idx]
[1]  1  3 NA  3  3  4  5  1  2

... and there's not allowed to be an NA in here. That's as far as I've gotten because I don't actually follow the logic of what this function is doing or what that's supposed to represent. But at least I've located the error!

Moving on, now. If anyone wants to figure this out I'm happy to send my code :)

  missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed

tmp[ cbind(REP$row[idx], REP$col[idx]) ] <- parTable2$free[idx]

[1]  1  3 NA  3  3  4  5  1  2

Moving on, now. If anyone wants to figure this out I'm happy to send my code :) 
 

On Tue, Aug 11, 2020 at 5:59 AM Edward Rigdon <edward...@gmail.com> wrote:
Mijke--
     OK, that didn't work, and I'm fishing. These are fully standardized parameter estimates, yes? Which would mean that the factors have variances of 1.      OK, that didn't work, and I'm fishing. These are fully standardized parameter estimates, yes? Which would mean that the factors have variances of 1. (What do the estimated variances look like in the solution, when you get this error message?) What if you set those factor variances to 1 explicitly? Sure, you DF will be off by the number of fixed parameter estimates. But if this doesn't work, then I'm thinking you (or Gignac) have a typo that has escaped our eyes.      In Model 2, SWLS is just another indicator of EI, with residual covariances, even though it has been swung to the right. It is hard to intuit with such a complex model.

On Mon, Aug 10, 2020 at 11:51 AM Edward Rigdon <edward...@gmail.com> wrote:
Mijke--
     There is a strong risk of empirical underidentification here, and the problem might crop up during iterative estimation. You might sidestep that using starting values, and maybe Gignac's final estimates would work as starting values for you. However, if any of the three loadings on TAS are smaller than Gignac's lowest 0.31, then identification may well fail, particularly at your low n.
--Ed Rigdon

What is going on here is that lavaan can not map this parameter to one
of the model matrices. In particular, the line

SWLS ~ EI

should be removed, and SWLS should just be another indicator of EI.

(A more informative error message would have been nice, though).

Yves.
